corpus_definition: To have a doctor cut open your body to fix something.
usage_note: have an operation + on + body part: 'have an operation on your knee'; have an operation + for + illness: 'have an operation for a heart problem'. The doctor operates; the patient has the operation.

relations.note: Same meaning; surgery is the medical word for operations.
Same meaning, but passive: 'She was operated on yesterday.'
Formal, used in news and by doctors.

context.text: My grandmother had an operation on her hip last month in Tashkent. The doctors say she will walk well again soon, but she is still nervous about having another operation.

reviewer_note: Fixed phrase; no forms. Usage note separates the patient (has an operation) from the doctor (operates).

corpus_definition: Dried grass used as food for farm animals.

forms.definition: grass that has been cut and dried to feed farm animals
forms.example: The horses are eating dry hay in the barn.

syn.note: Any dry food for farm animals, such as hay or grain.
Different: straw is the dry stems left after wheat or rice; animals sleep on it more than they eat it.
Easy word: hay is grass after it is cut and dried.

forms.note: No common verb. Farmers say 'make hay', not 'hay'.

context.text: Every summer my grandfather in Jizzakh cuts the grass and dries it in the sun. By autumn he has enough hay to feed his cows all winter.

reviewer_note: Compounds (haystack, hay fever) left out for the Compounds branch.

corpus_definition: A long period of very hot weather.

forms.definition: a period of several days or weeks when the weather is much hotter than usual
forms.example: The city suffered during the long heatwave.
forms.note: Also written as two words: heat wave (common in American English).

syn.note: A short period of hot weather; a little less strong.
Easy, general phrase; it does not say how long it lasts.
A long time with no rain; it often comes with very hot weather.

ant.note: A short period of very cold weather.

context.text: In July a heatwave hit Termez, and it was 47 degrees for a week. People stayed at home in the afternoon and went out only in the evening.

reviewer_note: Headword is a compound (heat + wave); heat and wave are not listed as its forms.

corpus_definition: The history, traditions, and buildings of a country.

forms.definition: the history, traditions and old buildings that a country has from the past
forms.example: Samarkand is an important part of Uzbekistan's heritage.

syn.note: Something left by people in the past; can be good or bad.
One custom or belief passed down; heritage is all of them together.
The way of life, art and customs of a people, now and in the past.
Easy word: everything that happened in the past.

forms.note: inherit (to get money or things from someone who has died) comes from the same old root, but it is not made from heritage.

context.text: Bukhara has more than a hundred old mosques and madrasas. The city works hard to protect its heritage, so tourists can still see buildings that are many centuries old.

reviewer_note: inherit/inheritance kept out as not_family (same Latin root, not made from heritage).

corpus_definition: a high area of land with hills and mountains

forms.definition: an area of a country with many hills and mountains
forms.example: The Scottish highlands attract tourists every summer.
forms.note: Usually plural. With a capital letter, the Highlands means the north of Scotland.

syn.note: Same idea, but the land is often less high and less wild.
Easy word: areas of high land, lower than mountains.
Very high land; highlands can have mountains in them.

ant.note: Flat land that is not much higher than the sea.

forms.definition: in or from an area with many hills and mountains
forms.example: We stayed in a small highland village near Chimgan.
forms.note: The singular form is used before a noun as an adjective.

syn.note: Having many mountains; describes the land itself.
Easy word: having many hills.

ant.note: In or from flat, low land.

people.definition: a person who lives in or comes from an area of hills and mountains
people.example: The highlanders keep sheep and goats on the hills.

context.text: Last summer we went to the highlands of Surkhandarya. In a small highland village, an old highlander showed us the way to a waterfall.

reviewer_note: Headword is plural; the singular highland is given as the adjective use (highland village).

corpus_definition: To make something easier to notice.

forms.definition: the most interesting or exciting part of something
forms.example: The highlight of our trip was the Registan at night.

syn.note: Same meaning, a little more informal.
The best or strongest moment; often about a career or a season.
The most exciting part of a story or film, usually near the end.

ant.note: The worst or saddest part of something.

forms.definition: to make something easy to see or notice, for example by marking it with colour
forms.example: Please highlight the most important parts of the text.

syn.note: Show that something is important; more formal. British spelling: emphasise.
Say that something is important, usually in speech.
Draw a line under words, or show that something is important.
Tell someone about something so they notice it.
Easy word: put a sign or colour on something.

ant.note: Make something seem less important than it is.

forms.definition: marked with bright colour so that it is easy to see
forms.example: Read the highlighted sentences again before the test.

syn.note: Has a sign or colour on it.

people.definition: a pen with bright ink that you use to mark words in a text
people.example: I used a yellow highlighter to mark the new words.

context.text: Before the exam, Dilnoza highlights the key words in her notes with a pink highlighter. The highlighted words help her remember the main ideas.

reviewer_note: Noun highlight (best part) kept as a same-family conversion: the part that stands out. Hair highlights not included.

forms.definition: an empty space inside something, or a low area in the ground
forms.example: The bird made its nest in a hollow in the tree.

syn.note: Easy word: an opening or empty space in something.
An empty space inside something; often used about teeth.
A place where the ground goes down a little.

forms.definition: the state of being empty inside
forms.example: You can hear the hollowness of the drum when you hit it.

forms.definition: to make an empty space inside something by taking out what is there
forms.example: We hollowed out a big melon and filled it with fruit salad.
forms.note: Usually used with out: hollow out something.

syn.note: Take out the inside with a spoon or your hand.
Make a hole by removing earth or another material.

ant.note: Put things inside until there is no empty space.

forms.definition: having an empty space inside
forms.example: The old tree trunk was completely hollow.

syn.note: Easy word: with nothing inside; empty is about a container, hollow is about its shape.
Curving in, like the inside of a bowl.
Lower than the area around it, for example sunken cheeks.

ant.note: Full of material all the way through, with no space inside.

forms.definition: in a way that sounds empty or shows no real feeling
forms.example: He laughed hollowly at his boss's bad joke.
forms.note: Belongs to hollow = (of a sound, laugh or promise) empty and without real feeling, not 'having nothing inside'.

context.text: The children found a hollow tree near the river in Chirchiq. They hid inside the hollow and pretended it was their secret house.

reviewer_note: Noun, verb and adjective all share the spelling hollow; hollowly kept as other_meaning (hollow sound/feeling sense).

corpus_definition: A large ring made of metal or wood.

forms.definition: a large round ring of metal, wood or plastic
forms.example: The girl played with a plastic hoop in the yard.
forms.note: In basketball, the hoop is the ring that you throw the ball through.

syn.note: Easy word for any round shape with a hole in the middle; a hoop is a large ring.
A round shape; a hoop is a real object in that shape.
A thin strip that goes around something.

context.text: At the circus in Tashkent, a dog jumped through a burning hoop. Then a girl spun five hoops around her body at the same time.

reviewer_note: Compounds (hula hoop) left out for the Compounds branch.

corpus_definition: A hard growth on the head of some animals.

forms.definition: one of the hard pointed things that grow on the heads of cows, goats and some other animals
forms.example: The bull had long, sharp horns.
forms.note: Horn also means the thing in a car that makes a loud warning sound, and a musical instrument you blow.

syn.note: A deer's horn, which has many branches and falls off every year.
A very long tooth, like an elephant's; not on the head.

forms.definition: having hard pointed things growing on the head
forms.example: A horned goat stood on a rock high in the mountains.

ant.note: Without any of these on the head.

context.text: In the mountains near Nurata we saw a wild goat. It was a horned animal with long curved horns, and it climbed the rocks very fast.

reviewer_note: hornet is not made from horn (people_not_family). Car horn and musical horn are other senses of the same noun.

forms.definition: a strong feeling of shock and fear
forms.example: She watched in horror as the car hit the wall.

syn.note: Very strong fear; horror has more shock in it.
A sudden bad surprise; not always with fear.
Easy, general word for being afraid.
Fear of something that is going to happen.

ant.note: A feeling of great happiness and pleasure.

forms.definition: to make someone feel very shocked and afraid
forms.example: The pictures of the flood horrified everyone.

syn.note: Easy word; horrify is stronger and includes fear.
Shock someone because something is very bad or wrong. British spelling: appal.
Make someone very afraid; less about shock.
Easy word: make someone afraid.

forms.definition: feeling very shocked and afraid because of something you see or hear
forms.example: She was horrified by the news of the accident.

syn.note: Very close; appalled is more about something being morally wrong.
Easy word; horrified is stronger.
Same idea, used in writing.
Very afraid; less about shock.
Easy word: afraid.

ant.note: Very happy and pleased about something.

forms.definition: very shocking and frightening
forms.example: The accident was a horrifying sight.

syn.note: Easy word; horrifying is stronger and includes fear.
Making you very afraid.
Very bad; often used for weaker things like weather.

forms.definition: very bad or unpleasant
forms.example: The weather in Tashkent was horrible yesterday.
forms.note: Belongs to the everyday, weaker meaning (very bad or unpleasant), not feeling shocked and afraid.

forms.definition: in a way that is very shocking and frightening
forms.example: The bus came horrifyingly close to the edge of the road.

syn.note: Easy word; less strong.
In a way that makes you afraid.

forms.definition: very badly, or very much in a bad way
forms.example: The plan went horribly wrong.
forms.note: Belongs to horrible = very bad or unpleasant, not feeling shocked and afraid.

context.text: Aziza was horrified when she saw the accident on the road to Fergana. It was a horrifying sight, and the horror stayed with her for days.

reviewer_note: Headword is a participle adjective; horror and horrify are the family's noun and verb. horrible/horribly kept as other_meaning (weaker 'very bad' sense).
